intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

selected_hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Then walk to the stunning Blue Mosque with its six minarets and intricate Iznik tile work. Hire a local guide to uncover the layered Byzantine and Ottoman history embedded in every corner.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Engage with vendors, taste free samples, and absorb centuries of trading culture in a single immersive half-day experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in a traditional Istanbul kitchen. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as meze platters, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), lamb kebabs, and baklava. Classes typically include a market visit to source fresh ingredients and conclude with a communal meal paired with Turkish tea or ayran.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the opulent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view sacred Islamic relics, and take a guided tour of the Harem — the private royal quarters — to understand the complex social hierarchy and daily life of sultans and their court.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, gliding between Europe and Asia while admiring Ottoman palaces, fortresses, and waterfront mansions (yalıs). After docking, explore the Karaköy waterfront for iconic Istanbul street food including fresh simit, balık ekmek (fish sandwich), and roasted chestnuts from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Istanbul Airport to Sultanahmet via the M1 metro + tram (approx. 90 min, ~80 TL). Check in to Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a relaxed orientation stroll around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) and the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı) with its ancient obelisks and monuments – all free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the narrow backstreets of Sultanahmet. Visit the rooftop terrace of your hotel or a nearby café for a first view of the skyline at dusk.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street cart near the airport or tram stop (~15 TL)
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi – iconic, budget-friendly köfte (meatball) restaurant on Divan Yolu Caddesi. A full meal with bread and ayran under 150 TL.

day_by_day.notes: Get an Istanbulkart transit card at the airport (reloadable, saves money on all public transport). Keep the first afternoon light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Ayasofya) first thing when it opens (entry is free, but arrive early to beat crowds). Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman calligraphy panels, and the vast dome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) – free entry for worshippers and tourists (dress modestly; scarves and shoe covers provided). Then explore the ancient Hippodrome and the German Fountain (Alman Çeşmesi) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Bosphorus shoreline at Kennedy Caddesi (Sahil Yolu) for sunset views. Return to Sultanahmet for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel (included if offered) or try a local börek bakery – cheese or spinach börek + tea for ~50 TL
meals.lunch: Çiğdem Pastanesi on Divan Yolu – grab a gözleme (stuffed flatbread) or a pastry for ~60–80 TL
meals.dinner: Dönerci Şahin Usta near Sultanahmet – a generous döner wrap with salad for under 120 TL

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is a functioning mosque; avoid visiting during Friday noon prayers. Women should carry a headscarf. Both major sites are within 5 minutes' walk of your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) – the heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Budget 3–4 hours. Entrance fee ~400 TL; Harem section costs extra (~250 TL) but is worth it. Book online to skip queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the First Courtyard of Topkapı to reach the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (İstanbul Arkeoloji Müzeleri) – one of the world's great archaeology collections including the Alexander Sarcophagus. Entry ~200 TL.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearby Gülhane Park (free) for a peaceful evening walk under plane trees. Watch locals play backgammon and sip tea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local muhallebici (milk pudding shop) – kazandibi or rice pudding + tea for ~60 TL
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapı Palace grounds – budget-friendly pide and soup option, ~150–200 TL
meals.dinner: Bab-ı Hayat restaurant near Gülhane – traditional Turkish home-style cooking (ev yemekleri), full meal ~150 TL

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace is closed on Tuesdays – Monday is a great day to visit. Wear comfortable shoes; the palace grounds are extensive. Gülhane Park is free and beautiful in May with blooming roses.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) – one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. Browse 4,000+ shops selling spices, textiles, ceramics, and jewelry. Free to enter; open Mon–Sat. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes downhill to the Egyptian Bazaar / Spice Market (Mısır Çarşısı) – a sensory feast of spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and teas. Free to enter. Pick up budget souvenirs like spice packets or lokum (Turkish delight).
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Eminönü waterfront district. Watch fishermen on Galata Bridge, browse the lively street stalls, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Simit Sarayı near Sultanahmet – simit, cheese, olives, and tea breakfast set for ~80 TL
meals.lunch: Tarihi Kapalıçarşı Pidecisi inside the Grand Bazaar – freshly baked pide with toppings for ~120 TL
meals.dinner: Balık-ekmek (fish sandwich) from a boat stall at Eminönü waterfront – iconic Istanbul street food for ~80–100 TL. Eat watching the Bosphorus.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Keep your belongings secure in crowded market areas. The walk from Grand Bazaar to Eminönü is downhill and very scenic – don't take a taxi.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Golden Horn via Galata Bridge (walk across – free!) to the Beyoğlu district. Climb the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) for panoramic 360° views of Istanbul. Entry ~300 TL – arrive early to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up Istiklal Caddesi (İstiklal Avenue) – Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century buildings, bookshops, cafés, and street musicians. Explore the side streets (Çiçek Pasajı, Balık Pazarı fish market).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the nostalgic red tram (T2) along Istiklal back toward Tünel. Explore Tünel and Karaköy neighborhoods, known for their artisan coffee shops and street art.

meals.breakfast: Van Kahvaltı Evi in Beyoğlu (or similar Kurdish breakfast spread) – a legendary spread of cheeses, honey, eggs, tomatoes for ~200 TL (worth the splurge, very filling)
meals.lunch: Balık Pazarı (Fish Market) off Istiklal – midye dolma (stuffed mussels) street snack ~5 TL each, plus a cheap sandwich, total ~80 TL
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası or a simple meyhane (tavern) in Karaköy – meze plates and bread, ~200 TL

day_by_day.notes: May 19 is Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day – a national holiday in Turkey. Expect some public celebrations and possible closures. The Galata area will be lively.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) – a stunning 6th-century underground Byzantine cistern with atmospheric lighting and the famous Medusa head columns. Entry ~350 TL. Located 2 minutes from your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sultanahmet neighborhood's lesser-known gems: the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi, ~100 TL), the Column of Constantine, and the Sokollu Mehmet Pasha Mosque – a masterpiece of Ottoman architecture, free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free Sound and Light Show at the Hippodrome (seasonal, check schedule) or simply enjoy a tea at a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) in Sultanahmet Park.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local kahvaltı salonu near your hotel – ~80 TL with tea
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Balıkçısı – simple fish restaurant near the cistern, grilled fish sandwich ~120 TL
meals.dinner: Develi Baklava & Kebap on Divan Yolu – try Adana kebab with lavash bread and ayran, ~180 TL

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern reopened after major restoration – it's more impressive than ever. Book tickets online to avoid the queue. The Sokollu Mosque is often overlooked by tourists and is beautifully peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Take the tram to Beyazıt and visit Istanbul University's historic campus gate area, then explore the Beyazıt Mosque (Beyazıt Camii) – one of Istanbul's oldest Ottoman mosques, free entry. Browse the secondhand book market (Sahaflar Çarşısı) next door.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Süleymaniye Mosque (Süleymaniye Camii) – arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque, built by Sinan for Suleiman the Magnificent. Free entry. Explore the surrounding neighborhood of the same name with its traditional wooden houses.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Süleymaniye neighborhood's rooftop cafés for golden-hour views over the Golden Horn and Bosphorus – one of the best free viewpoints in Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Börekçi Güllüoğlu near Beyazıt – freshly baked börek varieties for ~60–80 TL
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe restaurant in the Süleymaniye complex – historic Ottoman soup kitchen turned restaurant, affordable lunch menu ~150–200 TL
meals.dinner: Vefa Bozacısı (historic boza shop, since 1876) for a glass of traditional boza (~30 TL), then dinner at a local lokanta (canteen) in Süleymaniye – full plate meal ~120 TL

day_by_day.notes: Friday is the holy day in Islam – the Süleymaniye Mosque will be packed at noon prayer (around 13:00). Plan your visit for the morning or after 14:00. The Sahaflar book market is a wonderful cultural stop.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side (~20 TL with Istanbulkart). Explore Üsküdar's waterfront, the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, and the charming Çamlıca Hill neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Kadıköy – Istanbul's vibrant, bohemian Asian-side district. Explore Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı), full of fresh produce, cheese shops, delis, and street food. Browse the Moda neighborhood's café-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side via ferry from Kadıköy to Karaköy (~20 TL) – the evening crossing with city lights reflecting on the Bosphorus is magical.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a simit + tea from a Üsküdar street cart
meals.lunch: Kadıköy Market food crawl – try kokoreç (offal sandwich), fresh mussels, and a glass of şalgam (turnip juice), total ~150 TL
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy – a legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes. Full meal ~200–250 TL. Highly recommended for food lovers.

day_by_day.notes: Çiya Sofrası is one of Istanbul's most celebrated budget restaurants – featured in international food guides. The Bosphorus ferry ride itself is a highlight; sit outside on the deck. Kadıköy has a very different, more local vibe than Sultanahmet.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church / Kariye Mosque (Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood – home to the world's finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Entry ~200 TL. Take the tram + bus (about 30 min from Sultanahmet).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Land Walls (Istanbul City Walls) – 5th-century Byzantine fortifications stretching 6.5 km. Explore the towers and gates including Edirnekapı and Yedikule. Completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via tram. Visit the Arasta Bazaar (behind the Blue Mosque) for a relaxed browse of quality handicrafts at slightly lower-pressure prices than the Grand Bazaar.

meals.breakfast: Menemen and tea at a local kahvaltı salonu in Edirnekapı neighborhood ~80 TL
meals.lunch: Asitane Restaurant near Kariye Mosque – serves reconstructed Ottoman palace recipes, lunch set menu ~250 TL (a special splurge for food history lovers)
meals.dinner: Arasta Bazaar area kebab house – mixed grill plate with salad and bread ~180 TL

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church/Kariye Mosque has been under intermittent restoration – check current access status before visiting. The Theodosian Walls are UNESCO-listed and largely free to explore. Wear good shoes for the uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) – try Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584, near Sultanahmet) or the more affordable Çukurcuma Hamamı. Budget option: basic bath + scrub ~400–500 TL. A bucket-list cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi (Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts) on the Hippodrome – stunning collection of Ottoman carpets, calligraphy, and artifacts. Entry ~200 TL.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Cağaloğlu neighborhood – Istanbul's historic printing and publishing district. Visit Cağaloğlu Hamamı (one of the oldest hammams, worth seeing even just the exterior) and the surrounding Ottoman-era streets.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast spread at Sarı Konak Hotel café or similar – tea, cheese, olives, eggs, tomatoes ~120 TL
meals.lunch: Lezzet-i Şark on Divan Yolu – traditional Turkish home cooking, daily changing menu, full meal ~130 TL
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin near Arasta Bazaar – one of Istanbul's oldest fish restaurants, simple grilled fish with meze ~250 TL

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance online for better rates. Go early morning to avoid crowds. The hammam experience typically takes 1.5–2 hours. Çemberlitaş is 3 minutes' walk from your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) – a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara. Ferry from Kabataş (~50 TL each way). Visit Büyükada, the largest island – rent a bicycle (~150 TL/day) and explore pine forests, Victorian mansions, and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling around Büyükada. Visit the hilltop Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George (Aya Yorgi) for sweeping views. Swim at one of the island's small beaches if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul (last ferry around 21:00 – check schedule). Arrive back in Sultanahmet for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a simple restaurant on Büyükada waterfront – grilled fish or calamari with salad ~200–250 TL
meals.dinner: Simple lokanta near Sultanahmet upon return – lentil soup, bread, and a main dish ~120 TL

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are a beloved escape from the city. May weather is ideal. The ferry journey itself (about 1.5 hours) is beautiful. Buy ferry tickets in advance via İDO app. No cars on the islands – bicycles and horse-drawn carriages only.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş – the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore. Guided tour required; budget ~500 TL for both sections. Take the tram to Kabataş then walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront to the Çırağan Palace (free to view exterior – now a luxury hotel) and then to the Ortaköy neighborhood. Explore Ortaköy Mosque (Büyük Mecidiye Camii) beautifully situated by the Bosphorus, with the Bosphorus Bridge as backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Ortaköy is famous for kumpir (giant stuffed baked potatoes) – a must-try Istanbul street food. Stroll the waterfront and enjoy the lively atmosphere before returning via bus/tram.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or börek from a local bakery
meals.lunch: Simple café near Dolmabahçe – pide or lahmacun (Turkish flatbread pizza) ~100 TL
meals.dinner: Ortaköy kumpir street food – a loaded baked potato with multiple toppings ~150 TL, plus a waffle for dessert ~80 TL

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays – Wednesday is perfect. Book tickets online to avoid long queues. The palace is extravagant and very different from Topkapı – an interesting contrast. Ortaköy is very popular on weekends; expect crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – revisit your favorite spot in Sultanahmet at your own pace. Consider a last visit to Gülhane Park for a peaceful tea under the trees, or browse the Arasta Bazaar for any remaining souvenirs. Pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport via M1 metro from Aksaray or Yenikapı station (use your Istanbulkart). Allow 2–2.5 hours before departure. Return or top up your Istanbulkart balance at the machine (remaining balance is refundable).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast at a Sultanahmet café – the classic spread of tea, cheese, olives, eggs, honey, and kaymak (clotted cream) ~150 TL
meals.lunch: Quick midye dolma (stuffed mussels) or a simit from a street vendor near Eminönü before heading to the airport ~50–80 TL
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport (IST) is about 45–60 km from Sultanahmet. The M1 metro to the airport takes about 60–75 minutes and costs ~80 TL – far cheaper than a taxi (~500–700 TL). Refund your Istanbulkart deposit at a machine before boarding. Customs and security at IST can be slow – arrive early.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Istanbul Airport, clear customs, and transfer to your boutique hotel in Sultanahmet (approx. 45–60 min by metro/Marmaray or 60–90 min by taxi). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hagia Sophia from the square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet. Visit the Hippodrome (At Meydanı) to see the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column at dusk. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: N/A – grab a quick bite at the airport or upon arrival (try a simit from a street cart near the hotel)
meals.dinner: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi – iconic, affordable köfte (meatball) restaurant steps from the Hippodrome; budget ~150–200 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may set in. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport (Turkcell or Vodafone). Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs; better rates available in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya-i Kebir Camii) first thing when it opens to beat the crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its breathtaking Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history as church, mosque, and museum. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) – free entry, but note prayer times for closures. Afterwards, explore Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı), the nerve center of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Don't miss the Harem and Imperial Treasury (separate tickets).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to the waterfront at Eminönü. Watch the fishermen on Galata Bridge and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Browse the spice-scented streets near the Egyptian Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café – try menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) and çay (tea)
meals.lunch: Hafız Mustafa 1864 near Eminönü – classic Turkish pastries, börek, and light dishes at mid-range prices (~120–180 TRY)
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin in Sultanahmet – a beloved, atmospheric fish restaurant; grilled sea bass or bream with meze starters (~300–400 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays. Dress modestly for mosque visits – shoulders and knees covered; scarves available at entrances. Comfortable walking shoes essential.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı), one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. Arrive when it opens at 09:00 to enjoy it before the rush. Navigate its 60+ streets, 4,000+ shops selling ceramics, spices, jewelry, textiles, and leather. Practice your bargaining skills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Süleymaniye Mosque (Süleymaniye Camii) – arguably the most serene and architecturally magnificent Ottoman mosque in the city, with panoramic views over the Golden Horn. Explore the surrounding historic neighborhood of Süleymaniye.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Beyoğlu district via tram and funicular (Tünel). Walk up İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) – a vibrant pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century architecture, bookshops, music stores, and cafés. Explore the side streets (meyhane alleys) of Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Simit Sarayı on the way to the Grand Bazaar
meals.lunch: Şehzade Cağ Kebabı near the Grand Bazaar – try the unique cağ kebabı (spit-roasted lamb) from Erzurum; very affordable (~100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Meyhane dinner on Nevizade Sokak in Beyoğlu – choose any of the traditional taverns for meze platters and rakı; ~250–350 TRY per person with drinks

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Carry a map or use Google Maps offline – it's easy to get turned around inside. Keep bags in front of you in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums (İstanbul Arkeoloji Müzeleri) – a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient artifacts from across the Ottoman Empire, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) – the atmospheric underground Byzantine cistern with its forest of columns and famous Medusa head bases. Then walk through the historic Divanyolu (the ancient Byzantine Mese road) back toward your hotel, stopping at small Ottoman-era fountains and monuments.
day_by_day.evening: Take a sunset Bosphorus cruise – opt for a public ferry (İDO/Şehir Hatları) from Eminönü for an authentic, budget-friendly experience (much cheaper than tourist boats). Sail past Ottoman palaces, wooden yalı mansions, and the iconic bridges.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Khorasani Restaurant near Sultanahmet – excellent Anatolian cuisine including kebabs and lahmacun; ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası in Karaköy – a stylish, modern take on traditional Turkish lokanta food; ~300–400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeology Museums are closed on Mondays. The Basilica Cistern may have timed entry – book online. The public Bosphorus ferry (Boğaz Hattı) departs from Eminönü and is a fraction of the cost of tourist cruises (~50–80 TRY).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Asian side: take the Marmaray train or a ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) – a lively neighborhood market with fresh produce, cheese, olives, spices, and street food. Completely different vibe from the historic peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kadıköy's café culture and street art scene. Walk along the Moda coastline for lovely Bosphorus views. Visit the Moda neighborhood – a charming, bohemian area popular with locals. Take the ferry back to the European side in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) at dusk for panoramic 360-degree views over Istanbul. Explore the historic Galata neighborhood below the tower, with its narrow streets, independent galleries, and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast then grab a midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from a street vendor in Kadıköy – iconic Istanbul street food
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy – a legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes that change daily; a must for food lovers; ~200–250 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy area near Galata Tower – try Gram Restaurant for modern Turkish cuisine with a daily-changing menu; ~300–400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: May 19 is Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day – a national holiday. Some museums may be closed or have altered hours. Ferries and public transport run normally. The Asian side offers a refreshing contrast to the tourist-heavy historic peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) on the European Bosphorus shore – the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapi as the imperial residence. Its crystal staircase, Bohemian chandeliers, and European-Ottoman fusion architecture are stunning. Book a guided tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood. Explore the lively Beşiktaş market area and the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel, but the gardens are viewable). Continue to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for window shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a traditional Turkish bath (hamam) experience. The Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı offer authentic historical settings. Book the standard service (~400–600 TRY for bath, scrub, and foam massage).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş fish market area – grab a fresh balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from one of the market stalls; ~50–80 TRY
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant in Eminönü – rooftop terrace with Golden Horn views; excellent southeastern Turkish kebabs; ~300–400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires a guided tour and is closed on Mondays and Thursdays – IMPORTANT: verify current opening days before visiting, as schedules can change. If closed, substitute with a visit to the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) in Beşiktaş. Book the hamam in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Fatih district – the heart of historic Istanbul beyond Sultanahmet. Visit the Fatih Mosque (Fatih Camii) complex, one of the largest in the city, built on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles. Wander through the surrounding traditional neighborhood, still largely untouched by tourism.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque / Kariye Camii) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood – home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, rivaling Ravenna. Nearby, walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls (5th century AD) – the longest surviving Byzantine land walls.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn – a UNESCO-recognized area of colorful Ottoman-era houses, Greek Orthodox churches, and old synagogues. The neighborhood has a creative, slightly bohemian atmosphere with independent cafés and galleries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: A traditional lokanta (workers' lunch restaurant) in the Fatih district – point-and-choose from daily hot dishes; very authentic and cheap (~80–120 TRY)
meals.dinner: Fener/Balat neighborhood café or restaurant – try Fener Rum Patrikhanesi area cafés; Agora Meyhanesi in Balat for meze and fish (~250–350 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Note that Friday is the Islamic holy day – the Fatih Mosque will be busiest at Friday noon prayer (around 13:00); plan your visit around this. The Chora Church/Kariye Mosque may have restricted access if ongoing restoration continues – check current status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet – a beautifully curated collection of Ottoman carpets, calligraphy, ceramics, and manuscripts housed in the Ibrahim Pasha Palace. One of the most underrated museums in Istanbul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arasta Bazaar behind the Blue Mosque – a quieter, more authentic alternative to the Grand Bazaar, specializing in carpets, ceramics, and quality Turkish crafts. Good place for considered souvenir shopping. Then visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) adjacent to the bazaar.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening walk along the Sea of Marmara waterfront (Kennedy Caddesi) from Sultanahmet toward Kumkapı. Enjoy the sea breeze and views of the Princes' Islands. Kumkapı is a lively neighborhood famous for its fish restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Explore a traditional Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) spread – try Van Kahvaltı Evi in Cihangir for an elaborate Van-style breakfast with 20+ dishes (~200–250 TRY per person, worth the splurge)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the Arasta Bazaar – gözleme (stuffed flatbread) or a pide (~100–150 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kumkapı fish district – choose from dozens of competing fish restaurants along the pedestrianized streets; fresh catch of the day with meze; ~300–400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at most tourist sites. Arrive at the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum early. The Van-style breakfast is a cultural experience in itself – allow 1.5 hours. Kumkapı restaurants often have live music in the evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) – take a ferry from Kabataş or Eminönü to Büyükada (the largest island). The islands are car-free; rent a bicycle or take a horse-drawn phaeton carriage tour. Enjoy the Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada – hike up to the Monastery of St. George (Aya Yorgi Manastırı) for panoramic views of the Marmara Sea. Swim at one of the small beaches if the May weather permits. Browse the island's small shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to Istanbul in the late afternoon (allow 1.5–2 hours for the return journey). Arrive back in time for a relaxed dinner in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before catching the morning ferry
meals.lunch: Lunch on Büyükada – try one of the island's fish restaurants along the waterfront; fresh grilled fish with salad and bread (~250–350 TRY per person)
meals.dinner: Cooking Alaturka restaurant in Sultanahmet – charming, intimate restaurant serving traditional Ottoman recipes; excellent value (~250–350 TRY per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Büyükada run regularly from Eminönü (Şehir Hatları) and Kabataş; the journey takes about 1.5–2 hours. Buy an Istanbulkart for discounted ferry fares. The islands are extremely popular on weekends in good weather – go early. Check ferry schedules the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) in Beyoğlu – a superb private museum featuring Orientalist paintings (including the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey), Anatolian weights and measures, and excellent temporary exhibitions. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Cihangir neighborhood – Istanbul's most bohemian and artsy district, beloved by writers, artists, and expats. Browse the antique shops on Çukurcuma Sokak (a treasure trove of vintage finds), visit independent galleries, and soak up the neighborhood's creative energy.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Taksim Square and explore the streets around İstiklal Avenue at a leisurely pace. Visit the historic Pera Palace Hotel (Pera Palas Oteli) for a drink in its legendary bar – where Agatha Christie wrote 'Murder on the Orient Express.' A splurge-worthy experience for history lovers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Cihangir neighborhood – Ficcin Restaurant for traditional Circassian cuisine (a rare and delicious regional Turkish cuisine); ~200–250 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu meyhane – Refik Restaurant on Sofyalı Sokak, one of Istanbul's oldest and most beloved traditional taverns; meze and rakı; ~300–400 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Pera Museum is closed on Mondays – if so, substitute with the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy, which has a stunning new building. Çukurcuma antique shops are a highlight – allow extra time if you enjoy vintage browsing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) at Eminönü when it opens – explore the aromatic stalls selling Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, nuts, teas, and spices. A wonderful sensory experience and great place for food-focused gifts. Bargain respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry across the Golden Horn to Eyüp – one of Istanbul's most sacred Islamic sites. Visit the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and its surrounding Ottoman cemetery. Then take the historic cable car (teleferik) up to Pierre Loti Hill (Pierre Loti Tepesi) for sweeping Golden Horn views from the famous hilltop café.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Karaköy waterfront area for the evening. Explore the hip Karaköy neighborhood's independent restaurants, wine bars, and pastry shops. This area has undergone remarkable transformation and offers some of Istanbul's best contemporary dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast, then sample Turkish delight and dried fruits at the Spice Bazaar
meals.lunch: Lezzet-i Şahane near the Spice Bazaar – traditional Turkish dishes in an authentic setting; ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy Güllüoğlu – the legendary baklava shop in Karaköy for dessert; pair with dinner at nearby Antiochia Concept for southeastern Turkish cuisine (Antakya/Hatay region); ~250–350 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Pierre Loti Hill is named after the French novelist who frequented the café here. The cable car (teleferik) from near the Eyüp ferry dock makes the ascent easy. The Eyüp area is very traditional and conservative – dress modestly. Güllüoğlu baklava is a must-try; go after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Yıldız Palace complex in Beşiktaş – a sprawling late Ottoman palace set in beautiful park grounds. Less visited than Dolmabahçe, it offers a more intimate glimpse into late imperial life. The Yıldız Porcelain Factory within the complex is also interesting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Ortaköy neighborhood – a charming waterfront village beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Famous for its Sunday market (less busy on Wednesday), cute boutiques, cafés, and the picturesque Ortaköy Mosque right at the water's edge. Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (stuffed baked potato).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a final evening in the historic heart of Istanbul. Visit the illuminated Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia at night – they are dramatically lit and far less crowded than during the day. A magical way to say goodbye to the historic peninsula.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ortaköy waterfront – must-try kumpir (giant baked potato with numerous toppings) from the famous kumpir stalls; ~80–120 TRY. Add a waffle for dessert.
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant or a similar mid-range option in Sultanahmet for a final farewell dinner – try Ottoman-inspired dishes like lamb tandir or stuffed vegetables; ~350–500 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: The Yıldız Palace is less well-known but the park is lovely for a morning walk even if the palace itself has limited interior access. Ortaköy is very lively and photogenic – bring your camera for shots of the mosque with the Bosphorus Bridge in the background.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul – depending on your flight time, use this for any last-minute sightseeing or shopping. Revisit a favorite spot, pick up last-minute gifts at the Arasta Bazaar or a local shop (avoid airport prices), or simply sit in Sultanahmet Square with a çay and watch the city wake up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel (standard checkout is 12:00 – arrange late checkout if needed). Transfer to Istanbul Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights, plus 1–1.5 hours travel time from Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café – savour it: white cheese, olives, tomatoes, cucumbers, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), and endless çay
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout, or grab a simit and fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice from a street cart for a quintessential Istanbul farewell
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Pack any food souvenirs (Turkish delight, spices, tea, coffee) in your checked luggage to avoid customs issues. Keep a small amount of Turkish lira for tips, last coffees, and transport. The metro M11 connects the airport to the city efficiently. Wishing you a wonderful journey – İyi yolculuklar!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Private airport transfer arranged with luxury chauffeur service from Istanbul Airport to Sultanahmet boutique hotel. Check-in and settle into suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely orientation stroll through the Sultanahmet district. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque and the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı), soaking in the atmosphere of the historic peninsula without rushing into major sites on the first day.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Marmara Sea promenade near Sultanahmet Park. Enjoy the panoramic views of the Bosphorus and the illuminated silhouettes of the minarets at dusk.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at the hotel's rooftop restaurant or a nearby upscale café such as Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi for a classic Istanbul introduction.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Matbah Restaurant (inside the Ottoman Imperial Cuisine tradition, near Topkapı Palace) – a refined Ottoman tasting menu with mezes, slow-cooked lamb, and traditional desserts. Reservations recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm all upcoming reservations and private guide bookings with the hotel concierge. Request a welcome amenity briefing from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Topkapı Palace. Explore the Imperial Harem, the Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the sacred relics chamber with a specialist historian guide. Skip-the-line VIP access included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the adjacent Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya). Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, the massive dome, and the layered history of this UNESCO World Heritage structure. Private guide provides in-depth historical context. Follow with a visit to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) for its atmospheric underground columns and filtered lighting.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Sultanahmet. Enjoy a traditional Turkish tea ceremony at the hotel or a nearby historic tea house.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast spread at the hotel – cheeses, olives, sucuk, simit, fresh honey, clotted cream, and Turkish tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Istanbul at Sultanahmet) – Mediterranean and Turkish cuisine in an elegant former prison-turned-luxury-hotel setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Asitane Restaurant – celebrated for its meticulous recreation of historic Ottoman palace recipes, including dishes from 15th–17th century imperial kitchens.

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapı Palace Harem tickets in advance; private guide should arrange VIP entry. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Basilica Cistern may be cool – bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Private early-morning visit to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) before the tourist crowds arrive. Your guide explains the intricate Iznik tile work, the six minarets, and the mosque's architectural rivalry with Hagia Sophia. Followed by a walk through the Arasta Bazaar beneath the mosque.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex – three museums in one: the main Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk Museum. Highlights include the Alexander Sarcophagus and Babylonian artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus sunset cruise on a chartered wooden gulet. Sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, the Bosphorus Bridge, and the Rumeli Fortress with chilled champagne and canapés on board.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Deraliye Terrace Restaurant – Ottoman palace cuisine with views of the Sea of Marmara.
meals.dinner: Dinner served on the private gulet during the Bosphorus cruise, or disembark and dine at Mikla (Marmara Pera) for modern Anatolian-Nordic fusion cuisine with panoramic city views – arrange transfer.

day_by_day.notes: The Bosphorus cruise should be booked through a luxury charter company. Confirm weather conditions with the captain. Bring a light jacket for the evening on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) – one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. Your guide navigates the 61 streets and 4,000+ shops, focusing on authentic artisan workshops, antique dealers, and master jewelers rather than tourist traps. Opportunity to purchase premium Turkish carpets, ceramics, or gold jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Sample premium Turkish saffron, dried fruits, lokum (Turkish delight), and specialty teas. Cross the Galata Bridge on foot for views of the Golden Horn fishermen.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Karaköy and Galata neighborhood. Visit the Galata Tower for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul at dusk. Stroll through the atmospheric backstreets of Galata.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hamdi Restaurant (Eminönü) – famous for its southeastern Turkish kebabs and stunning Golden Horn views from the rooftop terrace.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nicole Restaurant (Tomtom Suites, Beyoğlu) – Michelin-recommended contemporary Turkish cuisine with creative seasonal tasting menus and exceptional wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Carry cash (Turkish Lira) for bazaar purchases. Negotiate respectfully – it is part of the culture. Comfortable shoes essential for cobblestone streets. Private guide can assist with authentication of antiques.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day private tour of the Dolmabahçe Palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus. Marvel at the 285-room Ottoman Baroque masterpiece, the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria), and the ornate ceremonial halls where Atatürk spent his final days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Beşiktaş district and the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi). Explore historic imperial caïques (royal rowing boats) and Ottoman maritime artifacts. Stroll along the Bosphorus waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam ritual. The Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584 by Mimar Sinan) or Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı offer premium private hammam packages including full-body scrub, foam massage, and oil treatment.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Feriye Lokantası (Ortaköy) – upscale Ottoman and Turkish cuisine in a restored 19th-century palace pavilion on the Bosphorus waterfront.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar (Ulus) – contemporary international and Turkish cuisine with stunning panoramic Bosphorus views. Private transfer arranged.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance and request a private suite for the most exclusive experience. Avoid eating a heavy meal immediately before the hammam. Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık and Harem sections.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex – arguably Mimar Sinan's greatest masterpiece. Explore the mosque, the surrounding külliye (social complex), the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and Roxelana, and the historic cemetery with its sweeping views over the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fatih and Zeyrek neighborhoods – authentic, less-touristed quarters of old Istanbul. Visit the Zeyrek Mosque (former Byzantine Church of the Pantocrator), a UNESCO-listed monument. Wander through traditional Ottoman timber houses and local bazaars with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Sufi Whirling Dervish ceremony (Sema). The Hodjapasha Cultural Center or the Sirkeci venue offer premium seating with cultural program notes. A deeply spiritual and visually mesmerizing experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Zeyrekhane Restaurant – set within a restored Byzantine building near the Zeyrek Mosque, offering traditional Turkish cuisine with extraordinary Golden Horn views.
meals.dinner: Pre-ceremony dinner at Khorasani Restaurant (Sultanahmet) – authentic southeastern Anatolian cuisine, celebrated for its Adana kebabs, meze selection, and warm atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for mosque visits (shoulders and knees covered; women bring a headscarf). The Sema ceremony typically lasts 90 minutes; VIP seating should be booked in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Princes' Islands (Adalar). Take a private boat from Kabataş ferry terminal to Büyükada (the largest island). Explore by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) or bicycle – no motorized vehicles allowed. Visit the historic Aya Yorgi Monastery on the hilltop for sweeping Marmara Sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada's charming Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and quiet beaches. Enjoy the relaxed pace, sea air, and island lifestyle far from the city bustle.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to Istanbul at sunset. Relax at the hotel or enjoy a quiet evening in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Packed premium breakfast prepared by the hotel, enjoyed on the private boat.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Miltos Restaurant or Ada Balık on Büyükada – fresh fish and seafood caught from the Marmara Sea, enjoyed with local rakı or chilled white wine on a waterfront terrace.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel rooftop restaurant or room service after a full day of exploration.

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are extremely popular on weekends – a private boat ensures flexibility and comfort. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and comfortable walking shoes. The island is ideal for photography enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood – home to the most spectacular surviving Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, depicting scenes from the lives of Christ and the Virgin Mary. A hidden gem compared to Hagia Sophia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Land Walls of Constantinople – a UNESCO-listed 5th-century defensive fortification stretching 6.5 km. Your guide explains the history of the 29 sieges these walls withstood. Visit the Yedikule Fortress (Castle of the Seven Towers) built into the walls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet. Enjoy a private rooftop cocktail experience at the hotel, watching the Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia illuminate against the night sky.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local neighborhood lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near Chora Church – an authentic, unpretentious experience guided by your local expert.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Balıkçı Sabahattin (Sultanahmet) – one of Istanbul's most beloved traditional fish restaurants, operating since 1927. Fresh Bosphorus fish, mezes, and rakı in a charming historic building.

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church may have restricted sections depending on restoration work – confirm access in advance. The land walls area involves uneven terrain; sturdy footwear recommended. Private car with driver suggested for this day's itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the vibrant Kadıköy district on the Asian side of Istanbul. Take a private ferry across the Bosphorus. Visit the Kadıköy Produce Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) – a sensory feast of fresh produce, cheeses, olives, spices, and street food beloved by locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the charming Moda neighborhood of Kadıköy – tree-lined streets, independent bookshops, vintage stores, and café culture. Visit the Moda Pier for Bosphorus views. Explore the Bağlarbaşı antique market if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by private ferry at sunset. Explore the Karaköy waterfront and the trendy Galata neighborhood for an evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Çiya Sofrası (Kadıköy) – a legendary restaurant celebrated internationally for its encyclopedic collection of authentic Anatolian regional dishes, many nearly forgotten. A culinary pilgrimage.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ulus 29 – perched on a hilltop in Ulus with breathtaking Bosphorus views, offering refined contemporary Turkish cuisine and an excellent wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is a wonderful contrast to the historic peninsula – more local, bohemian, and contemporary. The private ferry crossing itself is a highlight. Carry a light jacket for the ferry ride.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) on the Hippodrome. Home to one of the world's finest collections of Islamic calligraphy, Seljuk carpets, manuscripts, and ethnographic artifacts. The 16th-century Ibrahim Pasha Palace building is itself a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beyoğlu district and the famous İstiklal Avenue (Independence Avenue). Visit the historic Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage), the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market), and the Art Nouveau Pera Palace Hotel – where Agatha Christie wrote Murder on the Orient Express. Take the nostalgic Tünel funicular (one of the world's oldest underground railways, 1875).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical Turkish music concert or an evening program at the Pera Museum or Istanbul Modern (if scheduled). Alternatively, enjoy live fasıl music at a traditional meyhane (tavern).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pera Palace Hotel's Agatha Christie Suite Tearoom or the hotel's Orient Bar – a glamorous, historically rich setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal (SALT Galata) – one of Istanbul's most acclaimed restaurants, championing Anatolian ingredients in a sophisticated modern format with an exceptional natural wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is pedestrianized and can be busy on weekends. The nostalgic red tram runs the length of the avenue. Pera Museum requires advance booking for special exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a renowned Istanbul chef – learn to prepare a full traditional Turkish meal including meze (hummus, haydari, dolma), a main course (lamb güveç or sea bass in paper), and classic desserts (baklava or kazandibi). Held in a premium culinary studio or a private Ottoman mansion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Rahmi M. Koç Museum on the Golden Horn – an outstanding private museum of transportation, industry, and communications housed in a restored Ottoman anchor foundry and shipyard. Fascinating for history enthusiasts with exhibits ranging from submarines to vintage automobiles.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style luxury dinner at one of Istanbul's finest establishments – a celebratory meal with wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Enjoy the meal you prepared during the cooking class – a unique and personal dining experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Turk Fatih Tutak (2 Michelin Stars) – Istanbul's most celebrated fine-dining destination, offering an extraordinary tasting menu that reinterprets Turkish culinary heritage through a world-class modern lens. Book weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be booked through a premium culinary experience provider. Turk Fatih Tutak requires advance reservation – this is the unmissable dining highlight of the trip. Smart dress code applies.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Topkapı Palace Imperial Treasury and the newly restored sections of the palace complex not covered on Day 2. Alternatively, visit the Dolmabahçe Clock Museum or the Yıldız Palace and its surrounding park – a serene, forested Ottoman imperial estate in Beşiktaş.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ortaköy neighborhood – one of Istanbul's most picturesque waterfront villages beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse the weekend artisan market (if available), visit the ornate Baroque Ortaköy Mosque, and enjoy the vibrant café scene. Try kumpir (loaded baked potato) – Ortaköy's iconic street food.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell private Bosphorus dinner cruise on a luxury gulet – a romantic send-off with a private chef, white-glove service, fine Turkish wines, and the glittering lights of two continents reflected on the water.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell Turkish breakfast at the hotel – expanded spread with live cooking station.
meals.lunch: Lunch at House Café Ortaköy – a stylish waterfront café with international and Turkish dishes and stunning Bosphorus Bridge views.
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner aboard the luxury gulet during the Bosphorus cruise – customized menu featuring the finest Turkish seafood, mezes, and desserts paired with premium wines.

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner cruise well in advance through a luxury charter company. Confirm the menu and dietary preferences with the private chef. Bring a camera – the nighttime Bosphorus views are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Last stroll through Sultanahmet – revisit favorite spots, purchase any remaining gifts or keepsakes from the Arasta Bazaar. Visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) adjacent to the Blue Mosque if not yet visited – remarkable in-situ Byzantine floor mosaics from the Great Palace of Constantinople.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the hotel. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) depending on departure flight. Allow ample time for premium lounge access and departure procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the history, culture, and flavors of one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at the hotel – savor every bite of the cheeses, olives, fresh bread, and çay.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a farewell bite at a beloved café near the hotel before transfer.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport's premium lounge.

day_by_day.notes: Request late check-out from the hotel if the flight departs in the evening – most luxury properties accommodate this. Ensure all purchased items (carpets, antiques, ceramics) are properly packaged and documented for customs. Keep a copy of all receipts for tax-free shopping refunds at the airport.

query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026
